tier_reason: The numbers come from the peer-reviewed SC '25 paper (Zhang and Aiken, doi 10.1145/3712285.3759876); two independent search results quote its abstract (up to 11.7x QD, 34.4x CAMPARY, 35.6x MPFR, 41.4x FLINT) and name AMD Zen 5 (Ryzen 9 9950X) and Apple M3 Pro, but the paper hosts are blocked and the repo commits no results. The public harness (build_linux.sh: g++-14 / clang++-20 with stated flags; bench_linux.sh) would support A once the paper confirms CPU model and per-kernel numbers.

corrections.claimed_speedup: SC '25 paper abstract, as quoted by search results (paper not opened): peak performance up to 11.7x that of QD, 34.4x CAMPARY, 35.6x MPFR and 41.4x FLINT across the AXPY, DOT, GEMV and GEMM kernels at 2- to 4-term precision; which kernel, precision and thread count give each peak is unverified. The repo commits no result files.
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X (Zen 5) and Apple M3 Pro, per a search-result snippet of the paper (not opened); bench_linux.sh runs OMP_NUM_THREADS 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 with OMP_PROC_BIND=spread, OMP_PLACES=threads.

notes: Repo metadata confirmed: MIT (LICENSE, 2025 David K. Zhang), 2 stars, 2 forks, last commit 2025-08-27 'disable small-number optimization in FLINT' (stale is right); README is one line; multifloats/ holds MultiFloats.hpp and main.cpp. dl.acm.org and theory.stanford.edu (author PDF) were blocked. Record shortcoming: speedups are peak-vs-peak from a blocked paper; MultiFloats is not correctly rounded and runs hand-vectorized split-array kernels while MPFR/FLINT run scalar per-element calls.

tier_reason: benchmark/README.md states one core of an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v3, icpc 16.0.1 20151021 with -O3 -xhost -mkl (TurboBoost and SpeedStep off), and the figures (GETT_LoG_TTGT.png, benchmark.png) plot GETT against the MKL-backed TTGT and against max(CTF, naive) / max(CTF, TT, naive); the generator and benchmark scripts (benchmark/benchmark.py, ctf.py, eigen.py, tblis.py, libtensor.py) are public.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No numeric table; values read by eye from the figures. benchmark/GETT_LoG_TTGT.png, single precision, one Haswell core: abcde-efbad-cf GETT about 20.5 GFLOPS vs TTGT about 15 (about 1.4x, derived from figure); abcdef-dfgb-geac GETT about 55.5 vs TTGT about 25 (about 2.2x, derived from figure); on compute-bound cases TTGT ties or beats GETT (abcd-aebf-fdec about 67 vs about 75 GFLOPS single precision; in double precision TTGT leads on the last four cases, about 31 vs 37). benchmark/benchmark.png (Fig. 11): TCCG about 55 GFLOPS vs max(CTF, naive) about 13 on abcdef-dfgb-geac, and about 20.5 vs about 2 on abcde-efbad-cf (roughly 10x, derived from figure); near parity with the best other tool on the compute-bound cases. README text only says GETT is 'especially outstanding' for bandwidth-bound contractions.

notes: Figure values in the record match what the PNGs show.
